event: It is Sixthday; Nala wakes stiff in every muscle from yesterday's sifting and climbing.
At porridge the widow tells her rent for the week ahead is two marks, taken tomorrow morning.
Nala counts her purse under the table: four pennies. Two marks is twenty-four.
Wren sees her face and asks what is wrong, and Nala tells her.
Wren winces gripping the banister on the stairs, and tucks the bitten arm against her side.
Nala notices, and Wren says it only aches when she grips, and to stop looking at it.
Wren says Elowen's last paid night at the Kettle is tonight, and Elowen has nowhere after.
Wren says every room at Corbel House is let, but a second lodger sharing pays half a mark.
Nala looks at Wren, then thinks of her own narrow bed in room 7.
Wren grins and says it is Nala's room, so it is Nala who asks.
They find Elowen outside the Brass Kettle, with her pack already packed beside her.
Elowen admits she has eleven pennies and was going to ask the widow if she had a cupboard.
Nala asks her to share room 7, and stumbles over saying the bed is narrow.
Elowen says yes before Nala has finished, then goes pink to the ears about the bed.
They count it out at the corner table: two marks and a half is thirty pennies.
Nala has four and Elowen eleven: fifteen. They need fifteen more before the market shuts.
The market is closed on Restday, so whatever they find has to be sold today.
Nala unfolds her map and puts her finger on the chalk mark she made at the shifted passage.
She says the passage is new this spring, so its rubble may never have been sifted.
Wren stares at the map, then at Nala, and says that is a scout's thought.
Wren says they go down now, and stay until the dealer packs her baskets.
The warden signs the party into the Mouth book and notes the hour.
Elowen chalks fresh arrows down the Long Hall beside yesterday's.
At the shifted passage on the left, Wren goes in first, and they wait until she calls.
The passage runs narrow and low, and ends in a heap of fresh broken stone.
The rubble is sharp-edged, clean and free of dust: untouched.

event: Nala draws the new passage onto her map with a stub of Elowen's chalk.
They kneel at the heap and sift, lamps shuttered low, looking for the glow.
The first stone comes out of the heap within minutes; Elowen finds it.
The second and third come soon after; Nala finds both in one crack.
Wren tries to shift a big block one-handed, and gasps, and drops it.
Nala makes her sit, and says she and Elowen will lift, and Wren will pick the cracks.
Wren grumbles and does it, probing cracks with her bent pin and her good hand.
Nala and Elowen heave the blocks aside between them, shoulder to shoulder, sweating.
Elowen laughs when Nala's hair falls into her face, and pushes it back for her.
The stones keep coming, one and then another, small and warm and orange.
Nala keeps the count aloud: six, seven, eight, each time a little more breathless.
Twelve stones by late afternoon, and the rubble is picked down to the floor.
Nala works the sum out aloud: twelve at two pennies is twenty-four, less the guild's tenth.
They hurry back, following Elowen's arrows down the Long Hall at almost a run.
The warden signs them out and notes the hour, and they run up the ramp.
At the market the ember-stone dealer is tying the cloth over her last basket.
Wren puts the twelve stones on the counter and begs her for one more sale.
The dealer sighs, unties the cloth, weighs the stones and checks each in the light.
Twenty-four pennies; she holds back two for the guild's box and pays twenty-two.
Wren splits it on the counter: seven, seven, seven, and one over.
Wren pushes the odd penny onto Nala's pile, and says it was Nala's passage.
Nala has twelve pennies now, a silver mark's worth; Elowen has eighteen.
Together they hold thirty pennies: two marks for room 7, and half a mark for Elowen.
Elowen hugs Nala hard in the middle of Coppergate, and then hugs Wren, who yelps for her arm.
Wren twists four of her seven pennies into a scrap of cloth for Saltby.
The three agree they cannot spare four pennies each for the Kettle's supper tonight.
Wren buys a penny loaf with her own coin and says it is the party's supper.
They climb the back stairs of the Kettle to Elowen's room under the eaves.
It is tiny, the ceiling so low that Wren is the only one who can stand straight.
They sit on the floor and share the loaf, and Elowen's light sits on her fingers for a lamp.
Elowen says this is the last night she will sleep alone up here.

event: She goes pink at what she has said, and Wren laughs until she has to hold her arm.
Nala and Wren leave Elowen to her last night at the Kettle and climb Ladder Lane.
In the kitchen Nala tells the widow a second lodger is coming into room 7 tomorrow.
The widow says half a mark on top of the two, both paid in the morning.
On the top landing Nala checks Wren's bite; it is clean and closing, and Nala is glad.
Wren teases Nala that the bed in room 7 is barely wide enough for one.
Then Wren stops teasing, and looks at Nala a moment, and says goodnight, and goes in.
Nala lies in her narrow bed and measures it with her arms: barely wide enough for one.
Tomorrow night Elowen will be in it with her.
She thinks of Elowen's knee against hers, and of Elowen pushing her hair back in the rubble.
She thinks of Wren's look on the landing, and wonders what it meant.
She falls asleep with twelve pennies in her purse and her new passage drawn on her map.
A day in Emberdeep ends.
